_comment: Fleet-wide compose defaults merged into every service by engine.nix (see _shared/engine.nix:73-117 mergeSvc → lib.recursiveUpdate). A service's own composeSpec field overrides the corresponding default. Test gate: _shared/test-dist-v2.sh:105-150 asserts every field appears in every rendered docker-compose.yml. ─── init: true ─── Docker injects tini (~30 KB) as PID 1 inside every container; tini reaps orphaned children. Fixes the zombie-accumulation class of bug that caused Dagu's pids.max:256 saturation 2026-04-29. Containers with their own init system (s6-overlay, supervisord, systemd-in-container) override with init: false in their compose.nix. ─── logging max-size: 10m × max-file: 7 ─── ≈ 7 days of retention for typical low-traffic containers; high-traffic rotates faster (json-file driver is size-triggered, not time-triggered). Total cap per container: 70 MB. Per-VM disk headroom is bounded by disk-watchdog tiers at 85/90/95% (b_infra/_shared/modules/system-protection-watchdog-petter-dropbear-health-agent.nix).
_memory_limit_comment: Fleet memory CEILING policy, applied by _shared/memory-ceiling.nix (called from engine.nix's applyDefaults). NOT part of .defaults: a single fleet-wide number merged into all 57 services would cap a 16G gha-runner the same as a 48M redis. Instead every rendered container gets a ceiling from exactly one of three places, and there is no fourth: (1) its own compose.nix deploy.resources.limits.memory — which should read build.json containers.<role>.resources.mem_limit, the ONE declaration, see user-ai_kg-store; (2) by_category below, keyed on build.json's existing `category` field (the same classification the directory prefix and build.schema.json already carry — not a new parallel 'tier' concept); (3) it does not, and the BUILD FAILS. ─── why this exists ─── kg-store/kg-store-pub declared nothing, so docker stats showed them against the host total (23.41GiB) and SurrealDB's RocksDB sized its LRU block cache at max(visible/2 - 1GiB, 16MiB) ≈ 10.7GB. Measured oci-apps 2026-09-21: restarting both returned ~10.6GB. A cgroup cap is only half a fix — the ENGINE must also be told its budget, or the cap converts a leak into an OOM kill. ─── choosing the numbers ─── These are CEILINGS with deliberate headroom, not targets. Measured across all 58 running containers on oci-apps 2026-09-24 the largest resident set was languagetool at 899MiB and every uncapped container sat below 300MiB; the generous tiers go to the categories that host one-shot index/restore/backup jobs (data, obs) whose peak is bursty and unmeasured. A container that legitimately needs more declares mem_limit and wins — that is the override in (1). Test gate: _shared/test-kg-store-memory-ceiling.mjs.
_deploy_comment: Fleet-wide DEPLOY defaults, read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-ship-container-step-deploy-rsync.sh via get_config_array under the same key path a service's own build.json uses, so build.json:deploy.manifest_protect overrides it wholesale. Not merged by engine.nix (which reads only .defaults) and not part of any docker-compose spec. ─── manifest_protect ─── The reconciler deletes every remote file present in the previous deploy manifest and missing from the new one. .secrets, .secrets.json and .secrets.d are shipped by the secrets step, not by dist/, so a failed decrypt made them 'missing' and the reconciler wiped a running container's credentials; .dist-hash and .deploy-manifest are the deploy's own bookkeeping and are never rebuilt from dist/.
